subsystems.name: Motion sensor
subsystems.role: turns movement across a surface into digital X/Y motion.

subsystems.name: Scroll wheel
subsystems.role: scrolls vertically and often clicks sideways.
parts: optical or mechanical encoder with detents

subsystems.name: Control electronics
subsystems.role: converts sensor and button states into standard reports the computer understands.

subsystems.name: Housing and glide
subsystems.role: defines comfort, weight and how smoothly it slides.

buildSteps.title: Design the shape
buildSteps.detail: The shell is modelled in CAD from hand scans and ergonomic studies, then 3D-printed for test fits.

buildSteps.title: Design the circuit board
buildSteps.detail: A small PCB is laid out to carry the sensor, microcontroller, switches and radio, keeping the sensor close to the underside window.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the board
buildSteps.detail: Surface-mount components are placed and reflow-soldered; the optical sensor is mounted to tight positional tolerance.

buildSteps.title: Mould the parts
buildSteps.detail: Shell halves, buttons and the wheel are injection-moulded in ABS or polycarbonate, then painted or textured.

buildSteps.title: Write the firmware
buildSteps.detail: Firmware polls the sensor thousands of times per second, filters noise, scales motion to counts per inch, and reports over USB HID.

buildSteps.title: Assemble
buildSteps.detail: Switches, wheel, sensor and battery are fitted into the lower shell, the top shell snaps or screws on, and glide feet are applied.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and test
buildSteps.detail: Tracking is checked on varied surfaces, click force and lifespan are measured, and wireless latency and battery life are verified.

prerequisites.why: the sensor must photograph the surface fast enough to measure tiny movements.
wireless mice must run for months on a small battery.
a standard device class means no driver install — the mouse works on any modern computer.
shells need cheap, precise mass production with good surface finish.

pathway.milestone: high polling rates (1,000 Hz and well beyond) and lightweight shells with optical switches
pathway.unlocks: lower click latency and longer switch life for gaming and precision work.

pathway.milestone: wireless links matching wired latency at longer battery life
pathway.unlocks: wireless as the default even for competitive use.

pathway.milestone: onboard haptics and per-user shape or weight adjustment
pathway.unlocks: feedback and fit that suit individual hands and tasks.

pathway.milestone: tighter integration with headsets and spatial interfaces
